subject: Maths
title: Expanding double brackets
subtitle: Algebraic Expressions · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can expand the product of two binomials using the FOIL method or grid method.

key_vocab.definition: Expanding double brackets means multiplying two expressions like (x + 3)(x + 5) to remove the brackets and write as a single expression.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can expand the product of two binomials using the FOIL method or grid method.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Expanding double brackets -- Expanding double brackets means multiplying two expressions like (x + 3)(x + 5) to remove the brackets and write as a single expression.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiply each term in the first bracket by each term in the second bracket, then simplify by collecting like terms.
(x + a)(x + b) = x² + (a + b)x + ab
Middle term = sum, last term = product

Key examples:
  ✓ (x + 2)(x + 3) = x² + 5x + 6  (FOIL)
  ✓ (x + 4)(x − 1) = x² + 3x − 4  (mixed signs)
  ✓ (x − 3)(x − 2) = x² − 5x + 6  (both negative)
  ✗ (x + 2)(x + 3) = x² + 6  (forgot middle term)
  ✗ (x + 4)² = x² + 16  (must use FOIL)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – both positive
  Expand (x + 2)(x + 5)
  F: x × x = x², O: x × 5 = 5x, I: 2 × x = 2x, L: 2 × 5 = 10
  Combine: x² + 5x + 2x + 10
  Simplify: x² + 7x + 10
  = x² + 7x + 10
  (Collect the two middle terms: 5x + 2x = 7x.)

Example 2 – one negative
  Expand (x + 4)(x − 3)
  F: x², O: −3x, I: 4x, L: 4 × (−3) = −12
  Combine: x² − 3x + 4x − 12
  Simplify: x² + x − 12
  = x² + x − 12
  (Be careful with signs: +4 × −3 = −12.)

sections.title: One negative term
sections.content:
Expand and simplify. Watch the signs!

(a) (x + 5)(x − 2)
(b) (x + 3)(x − 4)
(c) (x − 1)(x + 6)
(d) (x + 7)(x − 3)
